question: A 21-year-old man presents to the emergency department with acute back pain. The pain began a few hours prior to presentation and is located on the left lower back. The pain is described to be “shock-like,” 9/10 in pain severity, and radiates to the left groin. His temperature is 98.6°F (37°C), blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, pulse is 101/min, and respirations are 18/min. The patient appears uncomfortable and is mildly diaphoretic. There is costovertebral angle tenderness and genitourinary exam is unremarkable. A non-contrast computerized tomography (CT) scan of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrates an opaque lesion affecting the left ureter with mild hydronephrosis. Straining of the urine with urine crystal analysis is demonstrated. Which of the following amino acids is most likely poorly reabsorbed by this patient’s kidney?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Left ureter lesion" -> "Poor reabsorption of amino acids" -> "Possible poor reabsorption of Lysine" -> 70% CHAIN: "Hydronephrosis" -> "Impaired kidney function" -> "Poor reabsorption of amino acids" -> "Possible poor reabsorption of Isoleucine" -> 60% CHAIN: "Costovertebral angle tenderness" -> "Ureteral obstruction" -> "Poor reabsorption of amino acids" -> "Possible poor reabsorption of Phenylalanine" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with left ureter lesion and hydronephrosis suggests impaired kidney function leading to poor reabsorption of amino acids. Given the possible poor reabsorption of Isoleucine in this context, Isoleucine is the most likely amino acid poorly reabsorbed by the patient's kidney.
